## C2 — Continuation facts, then confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: ABS versus pumping, front versus rear blowouts, blowout versus engine failure braking, brake failure steps and drop-off recovery
Continuation facts on preparedness, non-ABS braking, drop-offs, maintenance and breakdown reporting, plus confusable pairs among the emergency responses; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Most drivers will face an emergency sooner or later, and being prepared may let you prevent a serious outcome. [A01]
Why it matters: group preparedness; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
For most drivers the first instinct when a collision threatens is to stop the vehicle. [A01]
Why it matters: group braking; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
ABS braking means firm, constant pressure on the pedal, the opposite of pumping, which would switch ABS off. [A01]
Why it matters: group braking; confusable constant pressure versus pumping.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A02
If your vehicle has no ABS, follow your owner's manual for the right braking procedure. [A02]
Why it matters: group braking; confusable ABS versus non-ABS.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A02
A swerve has two steering moves: first toward where you want to go, then back the opposite way to straighten out once the problem is cleared. [A02]
Why it matters: group steering; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A02
Braking and swerving are not the only escapes, because speeding up may be what avoids a vehicle about to strike you from behind or the side. [A02]
Why it matters: group accelerating; confusable braking versus accelerating.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A03
Uneven surface drop-offs can cause serious collisions when a driver reacts the wrong way. [A03]
Why it matters: group drop-offs; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A03
Following the maintenance schedule in your owner's manual greatly cuts the chance of a vehicle problem while driving. [A03]
Why it matters: group maintenance; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A03
At a drop-off the safe response is a gradual slowdown and gentle steering back on, while the dangerous one is an immediate jerk back onto the pavement. [A03]
Why it matters: group drop-offs; confusable gentle return versus panic steering.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A04
A front tire blowout pulls the vehicle sharply toward the blown side, while a rear blowout makes it wobble and shake and pull only somewhat. [A04]
Why it matters: group blowouts; confusable front versus rear.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A04
After a blowout you avoid braking and let the vehicle coast down, while after an engine failure you brake with steady pressure rather than hard. [A04]
Why it matters: group malfunctions; confusable blowout versus power failure.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A04
For brake failure the parking brake comes first, and turning off the engine is the fallback only if the parking brake also fails. [A04]
Why it matters: group brake failure; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A05
For a stuck accelerator the printed order is engine off, then neutral, then an escape path, which differs from the restart attempt used after an engine failure. [A05]
Why it matters: group malfunctions; confusable stuck accelerator versus power failure.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A05
If you have a cell phone or other device, use it to tell authorities that your vehicle, or another one, has broken down. [A05]
Why it matters: group breakdowns; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A05
Flashers show your vehicle is disabled, while flares placed well behind it give approaching drivers time to change lanes. [A05]
Why it matters: group breakdowns; confusable flashers versus flares.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0107]

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
